larder:The auction at Palamós.name: The auction at Palamós
larder:The auction at Palamós.teaser: Be at the fish quay by half past four to see what the boats landed before you plan the galley's menu
larder:The auction at Palamós.story: For a galley, the Palamós quay is a briefing more than a shop. Stand above the auction floor late in the afternoon and you learn what came in today: how many crates of red prawn, which rock fish, what the swell kept in port. Then you know what to ask the fishmongers and restaurants for tomorrow. How the auction itself works is told on its own card in the tables.
larder:The auction at Palamós.why: Book the 30-minute guided visit and read the day's catch off the crates before you shop.
facts: The guided visit to the auction, then the day's prawn and rock fish in town
Auction Monday to Friday, late afternoon (about 4-8pm); guided visits at 4.30pm and 5pm in 2025 listings

larder:The anchovy shop at L'Escala.name: The anchovy shop at L'Escala
larder:The anchovy shop at L'Escala.teaser: Fillets in oil for this week, whole salted anchovies for the long passage: L'Escala's larder in a carrier bag
larder:The anchovy shop at L'Escala.story: Buy for how long you will be at sea. Fillets laid in olive oil are for the next few days, on bread rubbed with tomato. Whole anchovies packed in salt keep longest, and you rinse and fillet them yourself on board. Seitons, fresh anchovies marinated in vinegar, are for tonight; ask at the counter how each keeps. The house and its salting tradition have their own card in the tables.
larder:The anchovy shop at L'Escala.why: Take a tin of fillets for the aperitif and a salt-packed tin for later in the trip.

larder:The Lleó market at Girona.name: The Lleó market at Girona
larder:The Lleó market at Girona.teaser: In October the Girona market is about wild mushrooms: buy bolets, sausage and cheese before it shuts at two
larder:The Lleó market at Girona.story: Go in October for the bolets. The forest mushrooms of autumn come in on the stalls in flat crates, still with earth and pine needles on them, next to the botifarra and fuet of the charcuterie counters and the Empordà cheeses. The fish stalls carry the Roses and Palamós catch. Shop early: by early afternoon the shutters come down. Its own card in the tables has the market's story.
larder:The Lleó market at Girona.why: Buy whatever bolets are on the counter that morning and ask the stallholder how to cook them.
facts: Seasonal bolets (wild mushrooms), botifarra and fuet, Empordà cheeses, coast fish

larder:Espelt.name: Espelt
larder:Espelt.teaser: A large organic estate at Vilajuïga, now run by Anna Espelt, with a second vineyard above Cala Montjoi
larder:Espelt.story: Mas Espelt sits outside Vilajuïga, where the plain starts to climb towards the Rodes range, and the family's modern winery stands next to the old farmhouse. Under Anna Espelt the estate grew to about two hundred hectares across the Alt Empordà, all farmed organically for more than twenty years, which puts it among the largest growers of the appellation. A second property, Mas Marès, sits on the slopes above Cala Montjoi. The long visit walks the first organic vines planted at Vilajuïga before the glasses come out.
larder:Espelt.why: Do the long visit: the walk through the vines explains the wines better than the tasting notes.

larder:Mas Estela.name: Mas Estela
larder:Mas Estela.teaser: Vines among stone terraces in a valley of the Cap de Creus park, farmed by the moon since 1999
larder:Mas Estela.story: The Soto-Dalmau family, Núria and Diego, came to the Sant Romà valley above La Selva de Mar in 1989, bought an old farmhouse and farmed it organically from the first harvest. Ten years later they went biodynamic, working the vines to the lunar calendar with no synthetic inputs; their son Dídac now farms with them. The vines, about sixteen hectares, grow between scrub and dry-stone terraces inside the natural park, picked by hand. Some of the wine rests in clay amphorae. The names to know are Vinya Selva de Mar, Quindals and the two sweet ones, Moscatell Estela and Estela Dolç.
larder:Mas Estela.why: Ask for the amphora-aged bottles beside the oak ones; the comparison is the reason to drive up the valley.

larder:Martín Faixó.name: Martín Faixó
larder:Martín Faixó.teaser: Slate slopes on the hill above Cadaqués, inside the natural park, with the sea on three sides
larder:Martín Faixó.story: In 2000 the family behind Can Rafa in Cadaqués planted vines at Mas Sa Perafita, on the slate hill the road crosses before it drops into the village, at about three hundred metres and inside the Cap de Creus park. Their daughter Ester made the first wines in 2007. The tramuntana scours the slope and keeps the vines small; the bottles go out as Perafita and Cadac, with a Picapoll and a Muscat among them. The family spent two decades seeking permits to cut a cellar into the hill, and Ara reported in October 2025 that work would start in 2026.

larder:Empordàlia.name: Empordàlia
larder:Empordàlia.teaser: The village co-op at Pau where the Empordà's own olive, the argudell, becomes DOP oil
larder:Empordàlia.story: Empordàlia is what became of the old village cooperatives of Pau and Vilajuïga, and it still works out of the Pau co-op building on the Roses road, with the oil mill and the farm shop under one roof. Its oil, Oli de Pau, is a DOP Oli de l'Empordà pressed from argudell and corivell olives off the groves on the hills behind the bay of Roses: green, clean, with a peppery finish. ADN Argudell is the single-variety bottling. The visit walks the mill and the cellar and ends with four of the co-op's wines next to the oil.
larder:Empordàlia.why: Taste the argudell oil on bread at the shop and buy it by the can for the galley.

larder:Castell de Peralada.teaser: The appellation's best-known name: a medieval castle, a casino, gardens and a new winery for the visit
larder:Castell de Peralada.story: Perelada, the wine house, takes its name, in an older spelling, from the town of Peralada and its restored medieval castle, where the family business keeps a library, a museum, formal gardens and a casino. The range runs from cava through whites and rosés to the prestige reds and a sweet Garnatxa de l'Empordà. Visits now take in the new winery as well as the castle, in groups of no more than fifteen, and end with a tasting. The summer music festival in the gardens has its own card under Listening.

larder:La Vinyeta.name: La Vinyeta
larder:La Vinyeta.teaser: Vines, olives, sheep and hens on one farm at Mollet de Peralada, and natural wine to go with them
larder:La Vinyeta.story: La Vinyeta works the old Empordà farmhouse way, with vines, olive trees and animals on the same land: sheep graze between the rows and hens scratch through the soil, which Ara described in March 2025 as one of the most visited and best rated wineries in the Girona counties. Some wines are bottled with no added sulphites, and the farm sells its own olive oil and honey. The visit walks the vines and olives, tours the cellar and ends with a guided tasting; breakfast among the vines or a picnic can be added if booked ahead.

walks:Camí de ronda, Calella to Llafranc.name: Camí de ronda, Calella to Llafranc
walks:Camí de ronda, Calella to Llafranc.teaser: Half an hour of cliff path, steps and a rock tunnel between two coves, then up to the Sant Sebastià light
walks:Camí de ronda, Calella to Llafranc.story: From the boats at Port Bo the path heads north past El Canadell beach and onto the rock, cut into the cliff with steps and railings, pine roots running to the waterline. You hear the swell slapping in the clefts below and, in warm weather, the cicadas above. A short tunnel through the rock brings you round the point, past the steps of Casamar, and down into Llafranc's bay. From there a steeper climb leads to the Sant Sebastià lighthouse and a look back over both coves. Why this path was cut is told on its own curiosity card.
walks:Camí de ronda, Calella to Llafranc.why: Keep going up to Sant Sebastià; the view back over Calella and Llafranc is the payoff.

walks:Sant Martí d'Empúries to L'Escala.teaser: A flat seafront walk from a walled medieval hamlet, past the Greek and Roman ruins, into the anchovy town
walks:Sant Martí d'Empúries to L'Escala.story: Leave Sant Martí d'Empúries by its old walls and drop to the sand of the gulf. The path follows the shore south through pines, with small beaches on one side and the fenced ruins of Empúries rising on the other; the Empúries culture card tells what they are. Fishing boats sit off L'Escala ahead, and on a clear day the Gulf of Roses curves away north towards Cap de Creus. The walk ends at L'Escala's old quarter, where the anchovy shop and lunch wait.
walks:Sant Martí d'Empúries to L'Escala.why: Time it so you reach L'Escala hungry, with anchovies on bread as the reward.

walks:The Paratge de Tudela to the cape.name: The Paratge de Tudela to the cape lighthouse
walks:The Paratge de Tudela to the cape.teaser: A short loop through rock shaped like animals, coves of clear water, and a marked path on to the lighthouse
walks:The Paratge de Tudela to the cape.story: The Paratge de Tudela is the far end of the cape, where wind and salt have worked the dark rock into shapes people name: the most famous outcrop is S'Àliga, the Eagle, and Dalí borrowed these forms for his paintings. A marked loop leaves the car park on the cape road and passes viewpoints, S'Àliga and the coves of Culleró and Culip, the water below so clear you see the stones on the bottom. A connecting path through Mas Rabassers continues to the lighthouse, whose story sits on the Cap de Creus culture card. How old the rock is belongs to its own curiosity card.
walks:The Paratge de Tudela to the cape.why: Walk it in late-afternoon light, when the low sun shows every fold and hollow in the rock.

walks:Pals to the rice fields.name: Pals to the rice fields
walks:Pals to the rice fields.teaser: Down from the stone lanes and the clock tower of Pals into the flat rice paddies under the Montgrí
walks:Pals to the rice fields.story: Start among the stone lanes of old Pals and climb to the Torre de les Hores, the Romanesque tower, then walk out to the Mirador Josep Pla, where the plain opens below: the rice fields of the Baix Ter, flat as a table, ruled by irrigation ditches, with the Montgrí massif on the skyline. Rice has been grown around Pals since 1452. Lanes and tracks lead down among the paddies. In May and June they are flooded and mirror the sky; in autumn they lie cut and drained.
walks:Pals to the rice fields.why: Stand at the Mirador Josep Pla first; the whole plain makes sense from up there.

linger:Les Voltes at Port Bo.teaser: Whitewashed arches on the sand, boats pulled up beneath them, and nobody about before eight
linger:Les Voltes at Port Bo.story: Les Voltes is a row of fishermen's houses at Port Bo in Calella de Palafrugell, built over a run of low white arches that open straight onto the beach. Come at first light, when the flat-bottomed boats still lie on the sand in front, the arches are in shadow and the air smells of brine, wet pine and tar. In October the terraces are stacked away and you can sit on the sea wall alone with the gulls. On summer nights the same arches host the havaneres, which have their own card.

linger:Sa Tuna.name: Sa Tuna
linger:Sa Tuna.teaser: A few white fishermen's houses and hauled-up boats in a shingle cove below Begur
linger:Sa Tuna.story: Sa Tuna is a small cove of shingle at the bottom of a steep valley below Begur, with a few whitewashed fishermen's houses built close to the water and boats drawn up on the stones. Out of season it is very quiet: the slap of water on the pebbles, the odd fisherman mending gear. A short stretch of the coast path, with steps, climbs over the rocks to the next cove, Aiguafreda, and back. The road down is narrow and parking is scarce, so come in the morning, or arrive on foot.
linger:Sa Tuna.why: Walk the steps over to Aiguafreda and back, then swim in the clear water off the shingle.

linger:The square of Sant Martí d'Empúri.teaser: A shaded square inside a walled hamlet at the edge of the sea, a few minutes' walk from the ruins
linger:The square of Sant Martí d'Empúri.story: Sant Martí d'Empúries is a tiny walled village on a low rise above the gulf, and its square is its whole heart: the village church on one side, big shade trees, café and restaurant tables underneath. The first Greek traders settled on this rise before moving to the shore below, a story told on the Empúries card. Late in the afternoon the day-trippers go, the light turns gold on the stone, and a coffee here at the edge of the sea feels unhurried. In late October some terraces start to close for the winter.

linger:Jardins de Cap Roig.name: Jardins de Cap Roig
linger:Jardins de Cap Roig.teaser: A Russian colonel's castle and an English decorator's garden on a red headland above the sea
linger:Jardins de Cap Roig.story: Around 1927 Nicolai Woevodsky, a colonel exiled from Russia, and his wife Dorothy Webster, an English decorator, came to the cliff of Cap Roig near Calella and built themselves a castle. Dorothy laid out terraces of plants down the headland; by 1935 they held more than 500 species. In 1969 they handed the estate to the Caixa de Girona on condition it be kept, and the "la Caixa" Foundation now runs it, with sculptures by Jorge Oteiza, Jaume Plensa and Xavier Corberó among the paths. Find a bench above the water and read; the summer festival has its own card.
linger:Jardins de Cap Roig.why: Walk down to the lowest terraces, where the benches look straight out over the sea.

linger:Plaça de la Independència.teaser: Coffee under neoclassical arcades, a block from the river, between the market and the old town
linger:Plaça de la Independència.story: On the west bank of the Onyar, in the Mercadal quarter, the Plaça de la Independència is a closed rectangle of nineteenth-century arcades, every arch with café tables tucked under it. The arcades give shade at noon and shelter when it rains, so the square works in any weather. It lies between the Mercat del Lleó and the bridges into the old town, which makes it the natural halfway stop on a Girona morning. The old town itself is covered in the Girona guide.

linger:The Onyar bridges.name: The Onyar bridges
linger:The Onyar bridges.teaser: Stand on a footbridge over the Onyar and watch the ochre and red houses wobble in the water
linger:The Onyar bridges.story: The houses along the Onyar in Girona hang over the river in a long row of ochre, terracotta and saffron, a palette chosen when the façades were restored in 1983 and 1984. From the middle of one of the footbridges, the red iron one included, you see them doubled in the water, with the cathedral and the old town climbing behind. Early in the morning the river is still and the reflection sharp; at dusk the windows light up one by one. It costs nothing and takes a quarter of an hour. The Girona guide covers the old town beyond.
